characters.name: Hildred Castaigne
characters.description: First-person narrator of "The Repairer of Reputations", a man who becomes involved with Mr. Wilde and the Yellow Sign; claims a royal succession and is confined to an asylum.

characters.name: Louis Castaigne
characters.description: Cousin of the narrator; an officer whose intended marriage and exile are central to the narrator's plot.

characters.name: Dr. John Archer
characters.description: A physician who initially detains the narrator and later figures in the narrator's plans; a local doctor in New York.

characters.name: Mr. Wilde
characters.description: Eccentric Keeper of the 'Repairer of Reputations' business; scholar, manipulative organizer of conspiracies in the story.

characters.name: Osgood Oswald Vance
characters.description: A desperate client of Mr. Wilde who becomes involved in the narrator's scheme.

characters.name: Hawberk
characters.description: An armourer with a small shop in Bleecker Street; father of Constance Hawberk and acquaintance of the narrator.

characters.name: Constance Hawberk
characters.description: Daughter of Hawberk; a young woman involved (romantically) with Louis Castaigne; appears repeatedly in the narrative.

characters.name: Arnold Steylette
characters.description: Owner and Editor in Chief of the great New York daily; appears as a client of Mr. Wilde mentioned in the study.

characters.name: Colonel Livingston
characters.description: Military aide mentioned among dignitaries at the inauguration of the Lethal Chamber; present at public ceremonies.

characters.name: General Blount
characters.description: General commanding at Governor's Island; listed among officials at the Lethal Chamber inauguration.

characters.name: Major-General Hamilton
characters.description: Commanding the garrison of New York and Brooklyn; present at the Lethal Chamber inauguration.

characters.name: Admiral Buffby
characters.description: Admiral of the fleet in the North River; present at the Lethal Chamber inauguration.

characters.name: Surgeon-General Lanceford
characters.description: Surgeon-General of the National Free Hospital; speaks at the Lethal Chamber inauguration.

characters.name: Senator Wyse
characters.description: Senator of New York mentioned among dignitaries at the Lethal Chamber inauguration.

characters.name: Senator Franklin
characters.description: Senator of New York mentioned among officials present at the Lethal Chamber inauguration.

characters.name: Boris Yvain
characters.description: Young American sculptor whose marble group of the "Fates" and other works appear in various scenes; friend/acquaintance of the narrator(s).
characters.scope: THE REPAIRER OF REPUTATIONS; THE MASK

characters.name: Mr. Wilde's cat
characters.description: A vicious, recurring cat kept by Mr. Wilde; attacks and causes havoc in the Repairer of Reputations narrative.

characters.name: Alec
characters.description: First-person narrator of "The Mask"; sculptor/artist who recounts events concerning Boris Yvain, Geneviève, and tragic occurrences.

characters.name: Geneviève
characters.description: A model and sitter for Boris Yvain; central female figure in "The Mask" who becomes subject of romantic and tragic events.

characters.name: Jack Scott
characters.description: Friend of Alec and Boris; artist who appears across several stories (including as narrator in other tales); assists after Boris and Geneviève's deaths.

characters.name: Alcide
characters.description: A servant/house assistant mentioned in "The Mask" who packs and looks after the narrator's rooms.

characters.name: Marie
characters.description: Maid/servant who cares for Geneviève and appears in "The Mask" following her illness and death.

characters.name: Rosier
characters.description: Old Rosier, a country contact used to keep servants quiet after the tragedy in "The Mask"; a minor supporting figure.

characters.name: Monseigneur C——
characters.description: The preacher at St. Barnabé whose sermon frames the narrator's experience in "In the Court of the Dragon".
characters.scope: IN THE COURT OF THE DRAGON

characters.name: the organist
characters.description: A pale, slender man who plays discordant music at St. Barnabé and who becomes a persecuting figure aimed at the narrator.
characters.scope: IN THE COURT OF THE DRAGON

characters.name: Suisse
characters.description: A Swiss guard (Suisse) in rich uniform at St. Barnabé mentioned in the vespers scene.
characters.scope: IN THE COURT OF THE DRAGON

characters.name: Jack Scott (as narrator)
characters.description: Narrator of "The Yellow Sign" (first-person), an artist whose model Tessie Reardon reads the forbidden book and suffers tragic consequences.

characters.name: Tessie Reardon
characters.description: A favorite model of the narrator; naive and affectionate, finds a mysterious onyx clasp (the Yellow Sign) and later reads the book leading to tragedy.

characters.name: Thomas
characters.description: A bell-boy and attendant in the studio/building who recounts fears about the church watchman and later helps with deliveries.

characters.name: Ed Burke
characters.description: Also called Ed or Eddie Burke; brother of Lizzie; a young man mentioned as Tessie's suitor in "The Yellow Sign".

characters.name: Pinkie McCormick
characters.description: A girl in the model circle mentioned by Tessie; minor named participant.

characters.name: Lizzie Burke
characters.description: Friend of Tessie and sister to Ed Burke; minor named participant.

characters.name: Cabane
characters.description: Old Cabane, the baker mentioned in anecdotes about Rue and the watchman in "The Yellow Sign".

characters.name: the watchman
characters.description: A pale, repulsive church watchman whose presence unnerves the narrator and whose corpse is found later; central ominous figure in the tale.

characters.name: the doctor
characters.description: A physician who attends after Tessie's collapse and later comments upon the mysterious state of the dead watchman.

characters.name: Philip
characters.description: First-person narrator of "The Demoiselle d’Ys" (appears as 'Philip' in the legend), a stranger who meets Jeanne d'Ys on the moor and undergoes tragedy.

characters.name: Demoiselle Jeanne d’Ys
characters.description: The young noblewoman of the château d'Ys, beloved by the narrator Philip; dies tragically after a viper incident.

characters.name: Pelagie
characters.description: Nurse and attendant at the Château d'Ys who cares for Jeanne; a named supporting character.

characters.name: Glemarec René
characters.description: A piqueur (hunter's attendant) at the château; one of Jeanne's hunting retainers.

characters.name: Raoul
characters.description: A falconer serving Jeanne d'Ys; teaches and handles birds of prey.

characters.name: Gaston
characters.description: One of the falconers at the Château d'Ys.

characters.name: Hastur
characters.description: A falconer or bird-handler associated with Jeanne d'Ys' retinue (name used here in a falconry context).

characters.name: Sieur Piriou Louis
characters.description: A huntsman (sieur) in Jeanne d'Ys' household, named among the hunting attendants.

characters.name: Pierrot
characters.description: A theatrical figure appearing in the short pieces of "The Prophets' Paradise" (The Throng), used as a named character in the vignette.

characters.name: The Clown
characters.description: A stage/clown figure who speaks and appears in the vignettes collected under "The Prophets' Paradise".

characters.name: Severn
characters.description: An artist and painter; narrator of "The Street of the Four Winds" who rescues and feeds a stray cat and investigates its mysterious mistress.
characters.scope: THE STREET OF THE FOUR WINDS

characters.name: the cat (Severn's)
characters.description: A gaunt cat rescued by Severn in "The Street of the Four Winds"; wears a rose-coloured garter and leads him to its mistress.
characters.scope: THE STREET OF THE FOUR WINDS

characters.name: Sylvia Elven
characters.description: A mysterious woman associated with the north wing of the Severn's building (also appears as a central figure in other stories); her fate is tragic in Severn's tale and she is later central to other narratives.
characters.scope: THE STREET OF THE FOUR WINDS; THE STREET OF OUR LADY OF THE FIELDS

characters.name: Jack Trent
characters.description: American (Captain) and central character of "The Street of the First Shell"; husband of Sylvia, involved with the American Ambulance and the sortie scenes.
characters.scope: THE STREET OF THE FIRST SHELL

characters.name: West
characters.description: An artist (Monsieur West) friend of Trent and others; involved in social scenes and the siege narrative in "The Street of the First Shell".
characters.scope: THE STREET OF THE FIRST SHELL

characters.name: Braith
characters.description: A fellow student/artist who lives in reduced circumstances and is part of Trent's circle; present in the siege/night scenes.
characters.scope: THE STREET OF THE FIRST SHELL

characters.name: Fallowby
characters.description: A convivial, improvident man in the artists' circle; appears in Trent's dinner and siege episodes.
characters.scope: THE STREET OF THE FIRST SHELL

characters.name: Colette
characters.description: A young woman in the artists' circle; friend and hostess connected with West and the group's gatherings.
characters.scope: THE STREET OF THE FIRST SHELL

characters.name: Marie Guernalec
characters.description: A young woman in the artists' group who participates in the dinner and social scenes.
characters.scope: THE STREET OF THE FIRST SHELL

characters.name: Odile
characters.description: A young woman in the artists' party who attends gatherings and dinners in the narrative.
characters.scope: THE STREET OF THE FIRST SHELL

characters.name: Thorne
characters.description: An acquaintance in the artists' circle who is mentioned among the dinner guests.
characters.scope: THE STREET OF THE FIRST SHELL

characters.name: Hartman
characters.description: A man arrested as a suspected spy and for alleged profiteering during the siege; his arrest becomes a plot element in the sortie narrative.
characters.scope: THE STREET OF THE FIRST SHELL

characters.name: Captain Southwark
characters.description: An attaché of the American Legation (Captain Southwark) who assists in identifying and protecting an American detainee during the siege scenes.
characters.scope: THE STREET OF THE FIRST SHELL

characters.name: Père Cottard
characters.description: An old wounded man (concierge's husband) lodged at the pension; mentioned in Trent's concerns.
characters.scope: THE STREET OF THE FIRST SHELL

characters.name: Reverend Joel Byram
characters.description: An older moral guardian who helps Hastings find lodgings; solicits a respectable pension for the young student.
characters.scope: THE STREET OF OUR LADY OF THE FIELDS

characters.name: Hastings
characters.description: Young American art student and central figure of "THE STREET OF OUR LADY OF THE FIELDS" who courts Sylvia; experiences student life in Paris.
characters.scope: THE STREET OF OUR LADY OF THE FIELDS

characters.name: Madame Marotte
characters.description: Proprietress of the pension in the Street of Our Lady of the Fields who accommodates Hastings and other Americans.
characters.scope: THE STREET OF OUR LADY OF THE FIELDS

characters.name: Susie Byng
characters.description: A young American visitor staying at Madame Marotte's pension who befriends Hastings.
characters.scope: THE STREET OF OUR LADY OF THE FIELDS

characters.name: Mrs. Byng
characters.description: Mother of Susie Byng, an American visitor at the pension.
characters.scope: THE STREET OF OUR LADY OF THE FIELDS

characters.name: Foxhall Clifford
characters.description: Artist and social figure in the Latin Quarter; introduces newcomers and is involved in several romantic entanglements including interactions with Rue Barrée and Valentine.
characters.scope: THE STREET OF OUR LADY OF THE FIELDS; RUE BARRÉE

characters.name: Richard Osborne Elliott
characters.description: Artist and friend of Clifford, part of the Latin Quarter circle; appears frequently in social scenes.
characters.scope: THE STREET OF OUR LADY OF THE FIELDS; RUE BARRÉE

characters.name: Valentine Tissot
characters.description: A spirited, enigmatic young woman (Valentine) of the Latin Quarter who befriends Hastings and requests discretion about her private life.
characters.scope: THE STREET OF OUR LADY OF THE FIELDS; RUE BARRÉE

characters.name: Selby
characters.description: New student at Julian's and later protagonist of the "Rue Barrée" episode; becomes infatuated/curious about the enigmatic Rue Barrée.

characters.name: Rue Barrée
characters.description: An enigmatic woman known by the name of the street (Rue Barrée); a mysterious, reserved figure who is saluted by students and eludes exposure.

characters.name: the gardener (market)
characters.description: A flower-seller/gardener at the market who interacts with Rue Barrée and sells plants; assists with the delivery of Selby's flowers.
